title: Adapted Law Invariance and Time-Consistent Dynamic Risk Measures
summary: In static risk measurement, law invariance expresses the principle that the risk of a position should depend only on its distribution, and not on the particular probability space on which it is represented. In a dynamic setting, the same principle leads naturally to adapted law invariance: the risk assessment should depend only on the probabilistic structure of the financial position together with the way information about it is revealed over time. We show that, for time-consistent risk measures, adapted law invariance is equivalent to a recursive one-step conditional-law representation.…
